newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Text of Czech coalition economic recovery package.
newsitem.headline: Text of Czech coalition economic recovery package.

text.p: The following is a translation of an agreement by the Czech government coalition reached on Wednesday on economic measures aimed at reviving the economy.
The unofficial translation from the Czech original was made by Reuters:
STABILISATION AND RECOVERY PROGRAMME
OF THE GOVERNMENT COALITION
The retreat from an overvalued exchange rate of the crown, whose value did not correspond to the real efficiency of our economy, is the reckoning for a number of mistakes in economic policy.
Face to face with a currency crisis, we are obliged to clearly name its causes and look for ways for their removal.
The government must effectively react to the current situation.
The correction of economic policy and further transformation measures, approved by the government in April, did not catch all existing problems, and therefore it is necessary to go further.
The current economic situation is not only an accidental fluctuation, but it also reflects long-term trends and phenomena inside the Czech economy.

Among those belong low efficiency of the banking system, deepened by rescue actions by the state, bailout of ineffective activities from budget funds, extensive secondary payment inability caused by low effectiveness of the legal system, which prevents the enforcement of law, opaquess of ownership rights and the absence of of legal and administratrive measures in which it would be worthy for owners to be responsible.
The necessity of awareness of an early and widely discussed correction of shortfalls and unfavourable influences on the transformation process often did not lead to concrete solutions.

Those are the main factors which contributed to the evolution of a soft economic environment, non-existence of a proper business environmwent and capital market, and the survival of a large part of an inefficient corporate sphere.
The result of that is, apart from others, a faster growth of wages than productivity.

That caused extremely high domestic demand originating with personal consumption, which became -- along with high and fast growing investment -- the main source of the growing imbalance in external relations. The fact that the extent of openness of our economy is larger than some of our trade partners, contributed to that.

The declining competitivness of the economy was manifested by a gradual decline of economic growth and, from that, the resulting tension in the state budget and the trend toward an imbalance in public finances.
Low unemployment in this situation is rather a result of these unfavourable phenomena than an expression of a dynamically developing economy.

The parallel running of an extraordinarily high deficit of the current account of the balance of payments, problems with keeping the budget in balance, and political instability, necessarily had to lead to an attack on our currency.
This development was not set right in time, convincingly and fiercely.

The currency crisis of the last days, despite also having its speculative component which the Czech economy faces for the first time ever, showed the linkage of our economy to the world, the fragility and vulnerability of new economic relations, and the depth of our economic and above all balance of payment problem.

The unfinished dealing of our country with the transformation task and premature expectation of its end is being reflected in it, as well as the fact that the liberalisation and deregulation steps taken were not accompanied by appropriate ands legal protection.
Thanks to that it is possible today to use free competition for illegal purposes.
These omissions, failures and inconsistencies and the necessity to solve the consequences of today's currency crisis lead to our transformation path being longer than we expected and wished.

An important signal of the evolving economic imbalance has been the growing foreign trade deficit, growing for already two years, demonstrating the inability of our exports to compensate for fast-growing imports of investments and consumer goods.
We have to resist this now in a much more dramatic moment than would have been possible several weeks or months ago.

Despite all that, the Czech Republic has created high credit in the world in the whole period since November 1989, which we must not waste at this moment. And that's why today's measures must be consistent, radical, and unfortunately, also painful.
The current situation represents at the same time a chance for a remedy.

It requires adoption of short-term economic measures which will stop the decline of the crown and will lead to a stabilisation of the situation in the horizon of several months. Among these immediate measures belong -- above the currently realised measures of the April package -- these as the most important ones:

* further lowering of expenditures of the 1997 state budget in the areas of state administration, as well as investments, social transfers with the aim of balanced public budgets; prepare a slightly surplus 1998 budget;

* support of the consistent restrictive policy of the Czech National Bank (CNB) in its effort to minimise the increase of inflation and to lower the deficit of the current account of the balance of payments;
* strenghten the stability of the Czech currency through suitable foreign exchange measures of the CNB;
* implement uncompromising restriction of imports financed from public budgets;

* through negotiations with (government, unions, and employers) achieve their maximum possible wage temperance with the aim to avoid the development of dangerous wage, price and exchange rate spirals;
* freeze the amount of wages in the budgetary sphere;

If the measures -- implementation of a fluctuating exchange rate, which will secure finding a balanced rate level and restriction of aggregate demand -- do not secure in the second half of 1997 a clear and undeniable change of the trends of foreign trade -- exports and imports -- flows, then we are not excluding more radical measures of an administrative type, including the already known forms of regulation of imports -- import tariffs, an import surcharge, non-tariff measures, etc.

At the same time, we are saying openly to the public what these stabilisation and recovery steps will mean in the near future. A lowering of public spending, tightening of the environment in banking and credit area and a fast and effective recouping of debts in the private sector will lead to a temporary economic inhibition. Instead of growth of the ecomony we have to expect rather an economic decline, accompanied by a significant growth of unemployment. The changed exchange rate will cause a temporary increase of inflation. All of these phenomena will mean a decline of real wages and other income.

However the parties of the government coalition are convinced that it is not an easy one, but the fastest and therefore the least painful way toward repeated political and economic stability and growth. The coalition parties at the same time realise that only their unified and energetic proceedings and elimination of the crisis and its consequences in the shortest possible time will retain their mandate to direct the issues of this country.
(SIGNED) VACLAV KLAUS, ODS (Civic Democratic Party) MICHAEL ZANTOVSKY, ODA (Civic Democratic Alliance) JOSEF LUX, KDU-CSL (Christian Democratic Union - Czechoslovak People's Party) (TEXT ENDS)
